name: The deck wins against the competitive set it chose, which is not the one buyers use
description: An anchoring case. The deck names two specialist vendors and reports winning 7 of 10 head-to-head evaluations against them, calling that its clearest evidence of product quality. The corpus says those two vendors together hold 6-9% of agricultural employers, that the common shortlist is the incumbent farm-management ERP against a PEO [S1][S2][S3], and that vendor-reported win rates describe only the deals a vendor was invited into [S4]. The win rate is probably real and measures the wrong population. The only wrong answer is treating it as established evidence of competitive strength.

claims.rationale: 'supported' is the anchoring failure and the only excluded answer. The figure may well be true of the deals it describes; it says nothing about the majority of decisions where no specialist was shortlisted [S1][S4].

blind_spots.rationale: One half of the shortlist buyers actually use, absent from the deck.
The other half, adopted by default because it is already installed.
The specialist vendors' share, and what a vendor-reported win rate omits.
